newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to aim for MOF reform bill passage next year.
newsitem.headline: Japan to aim for MOF reform bill passage next year.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the government would aim to have its bills on Finance Ministry reforms pass through parliament at the next regular parliament session which begins in January.
"We plan to submit the bills by the deadline (for submitting bills to parliament) and aim for their passage during the regular parliament session," Mitsuzuka told a news conference.

Mitsuzuka said he and senior officials of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) would hold informal talks today at around 11.30 a.m. (0230 GMT) to discuss whether the bills would be submitted by members of parliament or by the cabinet.

He said they would take into account a policy agreement reached by the LDP, the Social Democrats and the Sakigake party, in which the three parties had agreed to devolve the supervisory functions of the Finance Ministry to an independent body.
The LDP has formed a minority government under Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto but has also made a loose alliance with the Social Democrats and the Sakigake party.
Mitsuzuka said he would like to create an opportunity to talk with Sakigake and Socialist officials on this topic soon.
He said he would like to discuss the issue of a supplementary budget at his meeting with LDP officials today.
"Economic conditions are an issue to look at (in forming the extra budget). It is important to look further into this," he said.
